I’m 47, and I weigh less now than I did in college, and it still feels “too much.” If the scale goes up even half a kilo, I panic. I check my stomach, thighs, hips in every mirror at the store, constantly thinking they look big, even though my coworkers tell me I’m “tiny” and customers sometimes ask if I’m okay.

I’ve cut out whole categories of food. I won’t touch bread, rice, pasta, oil, cheese, or anything I see as “fattening.” On breaks, I tell the staff I already ate, but really I just have black coffee or maybe a few carrot sticks. My doctor says I’m underweight and needs me to put some back on, but the idea of gaining makes me feel sick and terrified. I’d rather buy smaller clothes than even consider going up a size. All I think about is how flat my stomach is, how small my waist looks in the mirrors at work.
